headline: Football gets Dallas's calendar. The Mavs get October to December, then the heat.
summary: After a 26-56 season, Nico Harrison's firing and a Luka Doncic trade that still stings, this is a reset year. Interest peaks at the Oct 20 league tip-off, though Dallas's own opener date is still unconfirmed. It holds through the Cup and the holiday gift run, then fades once the Cowboys, Stars, Rangers and spring heat take over.

insights.title: Football owns fall, so the Mavs opener has to earn its slot
insights.detail: The Cowboys, Friday-night high school football, Texas-OU weekend at the Cotton Bowl during the State Fair of Texas, and TCU, SMU and UNT games fill every autumn weekend in DFW. The league tips off Tuesday, Oct 20. Dallas isn't on the national opening-night tripleheader or the Christmas slate, so its own opener date needs confirming. Early-season Mavs attention lives on weeknights and Cup Fridays.
insights.implication: Launch Mavs product in the opening week with weeknight and Friday Cup drops, and confirm Dallas's own opener date. Don't compete for Sunday football eyes. Borrow from Cowboys-season sideline culture instead of fighting it.

insights.title: Flagg is the first real jersey spike since the Luka trade
insights.detail: The February 2025 Luka Doncic trade and the Harrison era broke fan trust. Ujiri, May and Flagg are the repair. Interest in Flagg is the one draw that doesn't depend on wins. Irving's return from his ACL tear and Risacher's arrival are secondary pulls.
insights.implication: Open with Flagg-first Icon and Statement jerseys and tees at the opener. Plan a second wave for any Cup run. Keep Dirk heritage product as a parallel line, not a competing one.

insights.title: NBA Cup Fridays anchor the early season
insights.detail: Dallas is in West Group A with Denver, Houston, Phoenix and Utah. It opens Oct 30 at home against Houston, the in-state rival that gives Dallas a Texas-pride storyline. Utah visits Nov 6, then Dallas plays at Denver Nov 24 and at Phoenix Nov 27. Knockouts run Dec 4 to Dec 11 and stream on Prime Video, with semifinals at the higher seed's arena.
insights.implication: Build a Cup-night capsule and a Texas-rivalry (Mavs-Rockets) graphic moment. Hold stock for a Cup semifinal at American Airlines Center, which would be an unplanned window.

insights.title: Spring belongs to the Stars and Rangers when the Mavs miss
insights.detail: After last year's 26-56 finish, and with a 34.5 win total, April-June attention shifts to Stars playoff runs, Rangers baseball at Globe Life Field, FC Dallas and the Dallas Wings. The Mavs return only for the lottery (May) and the draft (June).
insights.implication: Don't plan playoff gear as the base case. Budget for a late push only if the team is in the Play-In picture (Apr 13-16). Plan a lottery and draft-night moment instead.

insights.title: Dia de los Muertos, Cinco de Mayo and Juneteenth are the city's cultural peaks
insights.detail: Oak Cliff and Bishop Arts mark Dia de los Muertos in late Oct and early Nov, which overlaps the Mavs' opening weeks. Juneteenth in Dallas falls near the draft, with Fair Park and Opal Lee's legacy of the holiday at its center. The Mexican-American community is central to DFW's identity well beyond the stadium crowd.
insights.implication: Pair community-led, creator-credited capsules with the Oct-Nov and June windows. Don't slap motifs on team product. Pay and credit Spanish-language and neighborhood partners.

insights.title: Heat decides when people shop and watch
insights.detail: Triple-digit summers from June to September push life indoors, and July-August is the low point for engagement. The first cool front in October arrives with the opener. Texas schools start in mid-August, so back-to-school beats the Mavs in late summer.
insights.implication: Keep Aug-Sep on lightweight, breathable training and lifestyle product tied to Flagg's training story, not game-day jerseys. Save the jersey push for the October cold front.

places.name: American Airlines Center
places.why: Home of the Mavs and Stars and site of the Dirk Nowitzki statue. It's the center of fan pilgrimage and of the arena planning conversation.

places.name: Deep Ellum
places.why: The live-music and mural district just east of downtown, where the creative and streetwear crowd gathers for game nights and gallery events.

places.name: Bishop Arts District
places.why: A hub for Oak Cliff's independent shops and Dia de los Muertos events, and a good fit for a locally owned retail pop-up.

places.name: Fair Park / Cotton Bowl
places.why: Home of the State Fair of Texas and the Texas-OU game each October. Together they dominate the weeks before the Mavs season.

places.name: Globe Life Field
places.why: The Rangers' home. Its summer and October baseball competes with the Mavs for the local sports dollar.

places.name: AT&T Stadium
places.why: The Cowboys' home, the center of the city's fall sports attention and the biggest rival for Sunday eyes.

people.name: Cooper Flagg
people.why: The face of the franchise and the reason the 2026-27 jersey and gift market exists.

people.name: Dirk Nowitzki
people.why: His statue and No. 41 are the permanent emotional anchor of Mavs fandom and heritage product.

people.name: Kyrie Irving
people.role: Mavericks guard returning from ACL tear
people.why: A veteran whose signature shoe sits outside Nike. His comeback storyline lifts early-season interest.

people.name: Masai Ujiri
people.why: The new front-office face. He built a community-rooted fan culture in Toronto, and Dallas will be watching for the same.

people.name: Dusty May
people.why: Fresh from the 2026 NCAA title at Michigan, he brings college-style energy and the Morez Johnson Jr. connection.

people.name: Opal Lee
people.role: Fort Worth educator and Juneteenth advocate
people.why: Her legacy anchors the June Juneteenth calendar across DFW, and she's a respectful reference point for community-led partnerships.

moments.why: Fair Park is the city's biggest autumn gathering. The fair likely closes a couple of days before the Oct 20 league tip-off.

moments.name: Dia de los Muertos
moments.why: Oak Cliff, Bishop Arts and Fair Park events overlap the NBA Cup's opening Fridays.

moments.name: NBA Cup knockout rounds
moments.why: The only chance for a meaningful December Mavs moment, and a possible home semifinal.

moments.name: NBA Draft Lottery and Draft
moments.why: The Mavs' lottery history makes this a high-attention moment even in a down year.

moments.why: A major Dallas cultural moment that overlaps draft season and calls for community-led events.

productHooks: Flagg-first opener capsule (opening week; league tips off Oct 20): jersey, tee and kids' sizes, dropped before the first home tip.
NBA Cup Friday capsule with a Mavs-Rockets Texas rivalry graphic, held in reserve for a semifinal run.
Holiday gift box (Black Friday through Dec 24) pairing a Flagg tee with Dirk heritage pieces for the gift-buying peak.
Draft-night and Summer League capsule in June-July, keyed to Morez Johnson Jr. and Flagg's second-year training story.
Lightweight, heat-ready training line for Aug-Sep that stays on-brand without game-day jerseys.
watchouts: Fan sentiment is still raw from the Luka trade. Skip nostalgia product that reads as taunting the current team or referencing Doncic.
Dia de los Muertos and Juneteenth imagery belong to their communities. Partner with, credit and pay local creators, and avoid sacred imagery.
Cowboys, Texas, Stars and Rangers marks are licensed separately. Don't blend them into Mavs graphics without clearance.
Clear Dirk Nowitzki's likeness and any City Edition story with the team and player licensing before use.
